title: 16-year-old girl gang-raped inside moving bus during 47-km ride to Delhi
content: A 16-year-old student was allegedly gang-raped inside a moving sleeper bus. She had boarded the vehicle seeking help while stranded in heavy rain. The driver and conductor then allegedly raped her and threatened her life. They abandoned the terrified teenager near Kashmere Gate bus terminal. Police arrested the accused and seized the bus for examination.

title: Babar Azam confronted over Pakistan’s alleged protest after Imran Khan interview
content: Pakistan captain Babar Azam firmly dismissed rumors regarding a potential protest by the team at Lord's. He emphasized his ignorance about any talks of the players refusing to come back after lunch. This controversy flared up following an interview on Sky Sports featuring Imran Khan's sons discussing their father's treatment.

title: ‘Beaten, eyes swollen, vomiting, dizzy’: Father on 3-year-old’s ordeal in school
content: A horrifying incident has unfolded at a Delhi playschool where a three-year-old boy reportedly endured physical and sexual abuse. Disturbing CCTV footage captures the child being restrained to a chair amid mistreatment. Following the event, his father noted alarming symptoms, including swollen eardrums, signaling urgent medical concerns. Authorities have detained one caretaker and are probing additional staff members.

title: Microsoft admits AI is making it tough to meet ‘environmental commitments’
content: Microsoft is taking significant steps to alleviate employee worries regarding the ecological footprint of its data centers. As the demand for artificial intelligence intensifies, the firm grapples with its promises to cut greenhouse gas emissions. In response to public criticism and local resistance, Microsoft is prioritizing innovative engineering and efficiency improvements, while also refining its approaches to renewable energy and carbon management.

title: Delhi cabbie sexually assaults 3-year-old nursery student, held
content: A cab driver employed at a Delhi school was arrested for allegedly assaulting a three-year-old student. The child identified the accused driver through photographs and CCTV footage shown by school staff. Police registered an FIR under the POCSO Act after the incident came to light. Preliminary investigation revealed the driver offered chocolates and assaulted the minor near a washroom.

title: Kharge venue 'purification' row: FIR against Rahul Gandhi for ‘giving caste angle’
content: An FIR was registered against Rahul Gandhi in Haldwani, Uttarakhand, on Sunday night.  He faces charges under BNS sections and the SC/ST Act for his statements.  A local resident alleged Gandhi gave a caste angle to routine cleaning work.  The complainant stated Gandhi's words hurt caste sentiments and incited hostility.  This development follows a purification ritual at a rally venue addressed by Mallikarjun Kharge.

title: Jilted man attacks ex-fiancée, her sister with acid in Hapur
content: A 22-year-old man attacked two sisters with acid after his marriage proposal was rejected. The victims sustained burn injuries and are currently in stable condition. Their father had previously agreed to the alliance but later called it off due to behavioral issues. The accused was arrested by police shortly after the incident occurred. Legal proceedings are now underway as authorities investigate the crime.

title: Starting September 1, Indian airports are discontinuing immigration clearance
content: From September 1, international travellers at Indian airports will experience a streamlined process for immigration clearance. The need for stamped boarding passes will be eliminated, allowing passengers to present either digital or printed passes. This change is designed to enhance efficiency and reduce wait times, as immigration officers will no longer stamp boarding passes during the departure process.

title: Developer bought 83 acres near Yosemite for $4m; US weighs land swap for road
content: A Nevada-based developer that bought 83 acres outside Yosemite for $4 million in 2024 is seeking a land exchange with the US government. The proposal could give the private property a direct road through a quarter-mile strip of Yosemite National Park. The same access plan was rejected in earlier legal battles, but the Trump administration is now considering it.

title: Travellers to Canada or those transiting through, here's authorisation you may need
content: Canada's immigration authority has revised its entry requirements for foreign travelers. Visitors may now need an electronic travel authorization (eTA) or a visa to enter the country. Citizens from eligible nations using air travel are required to secure an eTA. Additionally, US citizens and green card holders must adhere to specific entry regulations. It's essential for all travelers to meet fundamental health and financial criteria upon arrival.

title: Delhi's new fire safety rules: What property owners, developers need to know
content: In an effort to bolster city safety, new fire safety regulations have been implemented for buildings in Delhi. These updated guidelines, part of the Unified Building Bye-Laws, encompass eighteen crucial categories, including provision for fire engine access and secured exits. Additionally, structures are now required to maintain emergency power and continuous monitoring systems, all in response to recent fire incidents that highlighted the need for stronger protections.

title: Video: Powerful flash flood ravages Grand Canyon; 20 missing, 60 evacuated
content: A fierce flash flood surged through Arizona's Grand Canyon on August 29, transforming Bright Angel Canyon and the Colorado River into raging torrents of debris-laden water. Reports confirm that at least twenty people are missing following this alarming occurrence. Over sixty individuals were evacuated from Phantom Ranch and Bright Angel Campground, leading to the closure of affected park areas, with officials requesting assistance from the public.

title: Watch: Djokovic in tears during his first-round US Open defeat to Navone
content: Novak Djokovic was knocked out in the first round of the US Open by Mariano Navone in a four-hour, 36-minute five-set battle. The 39-year-old struggled with physical issues, including cramps and back pain, while making 70 unforced errors. Djokovic also became emotional during the match, with tears highlighting the frustration of a painful defeat and uncertain Grand Slam future.

title: Ankit Baliyan murder: 2 Gogi gang sharpshooters gunned down in UP encounter
content: Two suspected killers of singer Ankit Baliyan died in a police encounter early Sunday morning. The accused allegedly fired at police officers during a checking operation following Baliyan's murder. Police pursued the suspects, leading to an exchange of gunfire in the industrial area. Baliyan was shot dead outside a gym on August 26, with four assailants involved. Investigators are examining the suspects' potential role in the singer's fatal shooting.

title: Navy commissions INS Nipun, boosts deep-sea diving & submarine rescue capability
content: The Indian Navy commissioned INS Nipun, a new diving support vessel, in Mumbai. This vessel enhances deep-sea diving and submarine rescue operations for the Western fleet. INS Nipun joins its sister ship INS Nistar, completing a two-coast capability. Built domestically, the ship supports saturation diving and submarine rescue missions. It also features advanced medical facilities for deep-sea diving emergencies.

title: Gunmen chase bike, kill AAP man in Punjab; police suspect poll rivalry
content: In a shocking incident, an Aam Aadmi Party member was fatally shot while his friend sustained injuries in Mamdot market, Ferozepur. The assailants, armed and determined, pursued the victims on their motorcycle and fired at them. Rushed to the hospital, the party member was pronounced dead upon arrival. Initial investigations point to election-related rivalry as the possible motive.

title: Broad accuses Imam of ‘putting on an act’ after Pak batter ruled out at Lord’s
content: Stuart Broad raised eyebrows over Imam-ul-Haq's calf injury during the match, implying the Pakistani batter could be theatrical about his situation. Following a calf strain, Imam was unable to participate in the Lord's Test, while Pakistan faced another batting debacle, leading to a decisive loss. England triumphed, establishing a two-nil advantage in the series.

title: Rupee falls 13 paise to 95.56 as crude rises, Fed hike bets strengthen dollar
content: On Monday, the Indian rupee began its trading session lower versus the US dollar. The decline was influenced by rising crude oil prices and increasing geopolitical tensions. Furthermore, the prospect of a Federal Reserve rate hike has strengthened the dollar. In response, the Reserve Bank of India is taking measures to stabilize the rupee, while domestic stocks face downward pressure from foreign investors offloading shares.

title: US-Iran break weeks-long lull by targeting Larak island
content: In a sudden escalation, US forces targeted Iranian rocket launchers near Larak Island, disturbing an ongoing quiet period. Iran retaliated, showcasing missiles aimed at Jordan, where Jordanian forces successfully intercepted eight threats early Monday. Meanwhile, the US military noted Iranian efforts to deploy sea mines in the strategic Strait of Hormuz, contributing to a rise in oil prices as crude values surged after the military action.

title: Muslim law bars elder brother from selling minor siblings’ land: Gauhati HC
content: The Gauhati high court upheld a woman's land ownership acquired in 1975.  The court found the sale invalid for minor shares but acknowledged prolonged possession.  Family members challenging the sale were deemed late in their legal action.  The woman's continuous possession for over thirty years proved decisive.  Her successors are entitled to recover the land's possession.

title: Early dosage of statins could cut dementia risk by 15%: Danish study
content: A recent Danish study reveals that statins could play a role in reducing the risk of dementia among individuals with diabetes. The research analyzed data from more than 132,000 people, indicating that initiating statin therapy soon after a diabetes diagnosis may yield the most significant benefits. While statins are mainly utilized for cardiac health in diabetics, additional studies are necessary to confirm the drug's specific effects on dementia.

title: 3-year-old tied to chair, kicked and sexually assaulted at Delhi playschool
content: A young boy allegedly faced physical and sexual assault at a Delhi playschool. CCTV footage purportedly shows him being tied and kicked by school staff. Police have registered a case under Pocso Act and BNS against school officials. The Directorate of Education has also ordered a thorough inquiry into the incident. The child's father reported the abuse after noticing concerning behavioral changes.

title: Raksha Bandhan reunion ends in tragedy as truck kills 2 sisters in UP
content: A tragic accident near Etawah occurred when a speeding truck struck a motorcycle, resulting in the loss of two sisters' lives. The family was returning home from a Raksha Bandhan celebration when the horrific incident took place on Sunday. Alongside the fatalities, three individuals, including a six-month-old baby, were injured. The truck driver fled the scene, and police are actively pursuing him as part of their investigation.

title: Nepal floods: Hunt intensifies for 900 missing at hydel units, one tunnel head located
content: As rescue operations intensify in Nepal, over 900 individuals remain unaccounted for in the aftermath of devastating floods that have led to 810 confirmed deaths in both Nepal and Tibet. Teams are utilizing advanced tools at the Upper Trishuli-3A hydropower project to search for survivors. Notably, several Indian nationals are among the missing, which has led India to provide crucial technical and relief assistance for the ongoing rescue efforts.

title: Digital land records: How maps, drones and Bhu-Aadhaar are changing property identity
content: India is digitizing land records and creating unique digital identities for parcels. Over ninety-nine percent of land records are now computerized and georeferenced. A fourteen-digit identification number, Bhu-Aadhaar, is assigned to over forty crore land parcels. Drones are utilized for precise mapping of urban areas under the NAKSHA program. This digital land architecture aims to foster inclusive growth and formal credit access.

title: 'Pragg is No. 1 in the world': Anand after India's first GCT title | Exclusive
content: Praggnanandhaa has completed a remarkable comeback after his disappointing 2026 Candidates campaign, winning the Grand Chess Tour Finals in St Louis by beating Fabiano Caruana 15-13. He became the first Indian to win the title. Five-time world champion Viswanathan Anand praised his resilience and said, “I think at the moment, I would say he's the number one player in the world.”

title: ‘Losing $60 billion a year’: Trump slams Canada as ‘worst' trade 'abuser'
content: Donald Trump is escalating trade conflicts with Canada by levying substantial tariffs, which he claims are necessary due to the billions the U.S. allegedly loses from Canadian trade policies. He is urging Canadian firms to move their operations to the U.S. immediately. This action follows stalled trade negotiations, leading both Canada and the U.S. to impose retaliatory tariffs that affect various sectors and logistics.

title: Two Malayali women killed in California; friend detained
content: Two Malayali women were killed in California, United States, allegedly by a friend. Anjana from Thrissur and Ann Mary Mathew from Thiruvananthapuram are the victims. Police have taken the suspect, also Malayali, into custody for investigation. Ann Mary was reportedly stabbed while Anjana was knocked down by a car. Families are arranging to bring the bodies back to Kerala.

title: Iceland rejects EU membership talks, puts fishing rights and sovereignty first
content: Icelanders have decisively chosen to reject the idea of reopening talks for European Union membership. This choice reflects a strong commitment to maintaining national sovereignty and control over important fishing waters. While supporters believed this could enhance economic and security stability, critics were concerned about potential loss of independence. This referendum effectively concludes a prolonged discussion regarding Iceland's role on the global stage.

Adequate daily protein, proper hydration, sufficient sleep, and a consistent schedule are pivotal for muscle recovery and development. For those who exercise in the morning, a wholesome breakfast post-workout can provide long-lasting energy. Evening athletes should strategically plan their meals to enhance workout performance.

Shipping activities through the Strait of Hormuz have notably dipped due to rising tensions.

title: How to avoid rental disputes: Delhi Police plans awareness session for Northeast tenants
content: Delhi Police will host an awareness program next week for Northeast residents.  The event will focus on rental agreements and security deposit issues.  Tenants will learn about their rights and responsibilities regarding rent.  Police will widely circulate advisories with community leaders' help.  This initiative aims to prevent and resolve landlord-tenant disputes effectively.

content: The ICC has removed Sri Lanka’s hosting rights for the inaugural Women’s Champions Trophy in 2027 over government interference in Sri Lanka Cricket. The tournament will be moved elsewhere, with the venue yet to be decided. Sri Lanka could also miss out as hosts because they are ranked sixth. The ICC wants SLC to return to an elected administration.

title: Ahead of SCO, Uzbekistan joins India in condemning cross-border terrorism
content: Uzbekistan and India have elevated their relations to a comprehensive strategic partnership.  Both nations unequivocally condemned terrorism, including cross-border terrorism, in a joint statement.  This marks a significant diplomatic alignment on regional security dynamics and counter-terrorism efforts.  Leaders called for concerted actions against terrorist entities and disrupting financing networks.  They stressed holding perpetrators and their backers accountable for their actions.

title: Bizarre! Cricket team loses match due to broken print - here's how
content: Ballyspallen were forced to concede their Northern Ireland cricket match against Eglinton after a broken printer prevented officials from producing a required Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) sheet following rain. Eglinton had scored 159, while Ballyspallen were 19-0 when play stopped. League rules require the home side to concede if the DLS sheet cannot be provided to teams and umpires.
